q: For everyday use, the standard for measuring length may be a yard stick, ruler, _____ and so on.
e: For everyday use, the standard for measuring length may be a yard stick, ruler, metre stick and so on. The physics in this sentence is built around metre stick.

q: Lengths are usually measured in metre, centimetre or _____.
e: Lengths are usually measured in metre, centimetre or millimetre. The physics in this sentence is built around millimetre involving metre.
Greater lengths are measured in kilometre. The physics in this sentence is built around kilometre involving measured.

q: For measuring several metres (m), the suitable instrument is a _____.
e: For measuring several metres (m), the suitable instrument is a measuring tape. The physics in this sentence is built around measuring tape.

q: The accuracy of a measuring tape is _____.
e: The accuracy of a measuring tape is $1\text{ mm} (= 0.1\text{ cm})$. The physics in this sentence is built around $1\text{ mm} (= 0.1\text{ cm})$.

q: For measuring several centimetres (cm) to $1 ext{ m}$, the suitable instrument is a metre rule or _____.
e: For measuring several centimetres (cm) to $1 ext{ m}$, the suitable instrument is a metre rule or half-metre rule. The physics in this sentence is built around half-metre rule.

q: For measuring between $1 ext{ cm}$ and $10 ext{ cm}$, the suitable instrument is _____.
e: For measuring between $1 ext{ cm}$ and $10 ext{ cm}$, the suitable instrument is Vernier calipers. The physics in this sentence is built around Vernier calipers.

q: The accuracy of Vernier calipers is _____.
e: The accuracy of Vernier calipers is $0.1\text{ mm} (= 0.01\text{ cm})$. The physics in this sentence is built around $0.1\text{ mm} (= 0.01\text{ cm})$.

q: For measuring less than $2 ext{ cm}$, the suitable instrument is a screw gauge or _____.
e: For measuring less than $2 ext{ cm}$, the suitable instrument is a screw gauge or Micrometer. The physics in this sentence is built around Micrometer.

q: The accuracy of a screw gauge (Micrometer) is _____.
e: The accuracy of a screw gauge (Micrometer) is $0.01\text{ mm} (= 0.001\text{ cm})$. The physics in this sentence is built around $0.01\text{ mm} (= 0.001\text{ cm})$.
